<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **2** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **138** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 6dd99b82c38cd68b51c86241d53c5b7dda670a08` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 7d24d78f7cfbbe3f53afd64fb4eca19a8c32c9bb && git checkout 7d24d78f7cfbbe3f53afd64fb4eca19a8c32c9bb

git fetch origin 6dd99b82c38cd68b51c86241d53c5b7dda670a08 64bbd3693ef2f926e4f3d61920fbac5f2ee65913 && git checkout -B drift-repro 6dd99b82c38cd68b51c86241d53c5b7dda670a08 && git merge --no-ff 64bbd3693ef2f926e4f3d61920fbac5f2ee65913
```

</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `64bbd3693ef2f926e4f3d61920fbac5f2ee65913`
Local-runs: none

PR #21578 (`Part of #20234`, stage 11) at the head above, read against the card body and every comment on it, claim `5967611924`, dev report `5968433298`, ruling `5749154545` on #19123, the stage-10 landing `5903202064`, the net diff against `main` (3 files, +58/−30) and the head's check-runs. Read-only: no worktree, build, test or gate run. The cited commits and cards were read over `git show` in the checkout and REST.

**Scope against the claim and the ruling.** The claim names 2 form-C comments and 11 form-D rationale sites in the hand-written parts of `packages/spec/src/migrations/registry.ts`, "plus the tracker numbers in the explanatory paragraphs near them", then `gen:upgrade-guide`, one `@objectstack/spec` patch changeset, no gate touched, and it excludes the six census-pointer numbers (`5923089344`). The diff is exactly that: the 13 dead sites are gone (12 numbers; this review's own REST probe answers 404 for all 12, with the lit control #20234 at 200 and the dead control #8710 at 404), the 11 live numbers inside the same 9 rationale units are gone with them (form D: an author-shown passage carries no number), the 192 live author-visible numbers outside those units are left and counted, the six census-pointer numbers are untouched, the guide is regenerated, one patch changeset is added, and no script or gate changes. The scope reading is right.

### ① Derived judgments

**Text only — right.** All 11 hunks in `registry.ts` sit on string-literal lines (elements of the `step17.rationale` array, which is joined, and the `STEP18_RATIONALE[].text` concatenations) or on `*` / `//` comment lines. No `id:`, `order:`, entry, conversion id, export or code token appears on any added or removed line; the only structural change is two long string elements split across more lines inside the same initializer. Every hunk lies outside the six os-generated spans at head (1155–4974, 6341–20561, 20709–20934, 20944–24843, 24959–25089, 25100–26997): the rationale hunks fall at 341–6064, the docblock hunk at 6306–6314, the `//` hunk at 24941–24947. The dev's masked leaf-token proof (37,526 identical tokens, 6/6 controls) agrees with what the diff shows and is not needed to reach this reading.

**Form C, the 2 comments — right.** Both anchors are commits in this repository, `rev-parse --disambiguate` count 1 each, ancestors of `origin/main`, and each one's own subject names the number it replaces and the decision:
- base `:6301` `#8495` → `commit 4bfe1a539, PR #8666`. Subject: "refuse `${…}` placeholder syntax in memory persistence.path / persistence.key at publish (#8495) (#8666)". The sentence now says what was refused and where. The PR number stands beside the sha as a link, which the ruling allows, and it resolves as a pull request.
- base `:24935` `#6239` → `commit f549a0d4a`. Subject and body name #6239 as the ViewProtocol half of the 2026-08-08 ADR-0049 sweep; the `view-management-protocol-retired` entry the comment points at exists at head, and the comment's own "2026-08-08 sweep" matches the commit date.

Live numbers in the two edited comment paragraphs stay (#8336, #5295, #6414, #6486, all 200): form C reaches dead citations. #8336 moved onto an added line in the re-wrap and resolves.

**Form D, the 9 rationale units — each states its cited decision truly.** Checked against each commit's subject or body (for c459da6bc, 9e0ba21a1 and bc56e1881, whose subjects omit the number, against the number inside the commit's own diff: 8, 80 and 30 occurrences) and against the live cards read over REST:
1. Step 17 `mongodb` paragraph (`#6345`, `#4410`): e2798fab7 is "one driver vocabulary … mongo→mongodb (#6345)". cdf4d9a8a1 (#4410) first parsed `datasource.config` against the declared driver's contract, and its own table maps both `mongo` and `mongodb` to `MongoConfigSchema`, so "both accepted since `datasource.config` was first parsed against its driver's own contract" is true in substance and in sequence (2026-08-01, before the 2026-08-09 rename). The regenerated guide `:68` carries the same words.
2. `connector-error-mapping-retired` (`#14676`): 13c48c2a5 "retire connector.errorMapping … (#14676, ADR-0049)". Number dropped; the fragment already states the decision.
3. `form-view-option-default-removed` (`#12868`; objectui#6263 ×2, #7246, PR #7388): c459da6bc narrows per-option `default` out of the form-view vocabulary with the object-field face kept enforced; objectui#6263 records the maintainer ruling of 2026-08-28, option 甲, on the metadata-admin form renderer's analysis, with the rider that the console needs no second default contract. "Enforced there by a maintainer ruling of 2026-08-10" is PR #7388's own body executing the ruling on #7246 ("enforce"). "The console's form controls, none of which reads the key" is objectui#6263's finding. True.
4. `mapping-lookup-params-retired` (`#10329`, `#4509`): 15d58dbf1 retires the lookup steering params (#10329, ADR-0049); 5966c2abed (#4509) at 17.0.0 retired `mapping.extractQuery`, `errorPolicy` and `batchSize`. True.
5. `memory-persistence-placeholder-refused` (`#8336`, `#8495`): #8336 is the placeholder card whose refuse-at-publish direction landed as the protocol-17 entry `datasource-config-placeholder-refused` (connection-material driver config keys; at head `:2235`), and 4bfe1a539 extends it to the memory driver's `persistence.path` / `persistence.key`. True.
6. `metadata-customization-protocol-retired` (`#13135`, `#12057`): 9e0ba21a1 (2026-08-29) "Retire the paper metadata-customization protocol with its full coupling set"; #12057 is the finding it re-chartered, closed not_planned the same day. The kept words "ADR-0049 enforce-or-remove, maintainer ruling 2026-08-29" were already in the fragment. True.
7. `plugin-manifest-contributes-dead-members-retired` (`#10724`, `#10627`, `#10726`, `#11169`): be21955ba's body says #10627 measured, over three repos and controlled, exactly one non-test read of `manifest.contributes`, and that `kinds[].globs` went under the maintainer ruling of 2026-08-24; bc56e1881 later retired `routes` (ruled Option B) with the D3 entry `plugin-manifest-contributes-routes-retired`, present at head. "`routes` was left to a ruling of its own, which retired it as well" replaces a clause that was no longer true at head ("untouched pending its own fork"); the new clause is. True.
8. `stack-themes-carrier-retired` (`#10485`): 35ad101bc "Ruled B (退役授权面, 2026-08-21)". Number dropped; the fragment states the decision.
9. `translation-component-submit-label-retired` (`#10926`, `#9249` ×2): d173125fb "Option A per the maintainer ruling on #10926 (2026-08-22)"; #9249 is the `element:form` no-renderer card, and the `element-form-retired` fragment renders at order 8, before this one at order 14, so "retired whole above" holds. True.

**Regenerated artifact — right.** `docs/protocol-upgrade-guide.md:68` changes by exactly the step-17 words above and nothing else in the guide moves. `spec-changes.json` projects no step rationale, so it rightly does not move. No test, `content/docs/**` page or skill quotes a changed phrase; the old spellings that remain are live-number comments in other files, release-owned pages and test titles, all outside this stage.

**Numbers added:** one, `#8666`, a live PR beside its commit in a comment. No dead number is added, and no number is added to author-visible text.

**Check-runs on the head**, read at 2026-10-03T10:59Z: 33 runs, 26 success, 3 skipped (Build Docs, Console Pin Gate, Packed-tarball smoke), 4 in progress (Test Core 1/6, 2/6 and 4/6, Type Check · workspace), 0 failure. Check Changeset, Lint & Repo Gates, Spec property liveness, Build Core and the other three Type Check runs are success. The four in-progress runs are read as not concluded, not as passes; landing waits on them under the seat's pre-landing protocol. Nothing the diff touches (text inside strings and comments, one generated guide line) is a plausible cause for any of them to turn.

### ② Semver level

**`patch` — right.** `packages/spec` ships `dist`; the step rationales compile into `dist/migrations/*` and print to authors through `os migrate meta`, so the published text changes, while the two comments do not ship. No schema, export, accept set, migration step, entry, retired key or def, conversion or runtime behaviour moves, so neither `minor` nor `major` is in reach, and `skip-changeset` would under-declare a published text change. The changeset names `'@objectstack/spec': patch` and carries `Clause-②: no`; the PR body's `Clause-②: no` is right, since no accept set moves, and the ruling itself set `Clause-②: no` for these rewrites. Check Changeset: success.

### ③ Boundary flags

Dev flags (the deviations), each answered:
1. Scope reading — removing the 11 live numbers inside the 9 units is inside the claim's "numbers in the explanatory paragraphs near them" and inside form D; leaving the 192 outside is right (not claimed, not dead). Accepted.
2. Two clauses changed beyond deleting a number (`routes`; the #8336 refusal) — both verified true above; each writes the decision in words where the number alone had carried it. Accepted.
3. Live comment numbers stay — form C reaches dead citations; the four live ones resolve. Accepted.
4. Three derived gates first exited 3 for unbuilt dist and then 0 — reported, not hidden; CI's Lint & Repo Gates is success. Accepted.
5. Attribution — the three branch commits carry `Claude-Session` plus the model-free `Co-authored-by` trailer, read off `git log`, as AGENTS.md requires. Accepted.
6. Merge of `origin/main` 6dd99b82c3 through `os-regen-merge.sh` with no regeneration commit owed — consistent with the diff (the guide moves by one line) and with `check:generated` passing inside Lint & Repo Gates. Accepted.
7–9. No labels written; three pushes plus one empty probe and no force-push; worktree cleanup after the report — procedural, nothing to re-judge.

Open question (one): which card carries the 192 live author-visible numbers left in `registry.ts` step rationales — A, a next stage of #20234 split at the step boundary; B, #20749 lifts its "not this stage" exclusion; C, leave them.
- **C is refused by the ruling of record.** D says anything an author is shown carries no number, and the card body repeats it ("Anything an author is shown takes D (no number)"). These passages print in `os migrate meta` and, for step 17, in the published guide.
- **A or B is a staging and ownership call between two cards the same seat holds, so it is escalated to the `domain:spec` seat rather than decided here.** For the seat's reading: #20749's body already counts migration-registry text as its share and works under ruling `5902360492` (recorded on its parent #20513; form D for all author-visible text), yet both of its stage claims exclude this file as "#20234's stage 11", and #20234's charter is dead citations. Whichever card takes them brings its own census instrument: `check:doc-authoring` and the citation gate both blank these string positions, so the doc-authoring ledger cannot drive the end state here. The `migrations.test.ts` pin on the live #4722 moves with step 17.
- Not a blocker for this PR: the 192 are live, outside the claim, and reported with counts.

Out-of-scope findings (two), both carrier `none`: the citation gate reads comment prose only, and `check:doc-authoring`'s spec leg does not read step rationales, so the 11 dead sites were never in a census. A coverage boundary recorded the same way at stage 9; new gates default to no. Accepted as noted, not filed.
